articles.title: Navigating EMCA Cap 387 and Statutory NEMA EIA Licencing in Kenya
articles.author: Belinda Nyakinya, Managing Director
articles.excerpt: A practical guide for project proponents on the statutory steps, scoping studies, public participation, and lead agency reviews required under Kenyan environmental law.
articles.content: Under the Environmental Management and Co-ordination Act (EMCA Cap 387) and the Environmental (Impact Assessment and Audit) Regulations, high and medium risk infrastructure projects in Kenya must secure a statutory EIA Licence from NEMA prior to project commencement. This technical briefing details the preparation of comprehensive Terms of Reference (TOR), baseline biophysical and socio-economic characterization, public participation requirements, and the development of actionable Construction Environmental and Social Management Plans (C-ESMP).

articles.title: Bridging National Resettlement Protocols and World Bank ESS5 Standards
articles.author: HUERI Social Safeguards Practice
articles.excerpt: Best practices for aligning Kenyan land acquisition and valuation frameworks with international lender safeguard standards for Resettlement Action Plans (RAP).
articles.content: When delivering linear infrastructure, renewable energy installations, or urban redevelopment projects financed by multilateral lenders, project proponents must navigate the intersection between Kenyan statutory land compensation laws and international benchmarks such as World Bank ESS5 and IFC Performance Standard 5. This article outlines methods for conducting rigorous socio-economic baseline surveys, participatory asset valuations, livelihood restoration programs, and structured Grievance Redress Mechanisms (GRMs).

articles.title: Implementing ESHSRIM Procedures for Large Infrastructure Projects
articles.author: Technical Training & Compliance Desk
articles.excerpt: Structured risk and impact management procedures to equip project implementation units and resident engineers with auditable monitoring tools.
articles.content: Environmental, Social, Health and Safety Risks and Impacts Management (ESHSRIM) procedures provide a systematic framework for translating high-level commitments into everyday site monitoring routines. This briefing covers contractor compliance audits, hazard identification and risk assessments (HIRA), incident reporting hierarchies, and ongoing community stakeholder dialogue.
